title: Chapter 4 · Test 4
summary: Chapter 4 test 4: surds and the surface area and volume of pyramids, cones and spheres (15 questions).
body: This is Test 4 for Chapter 4: Measurement and surds. It checks all six lessons: simplifying surds, operations with surds, rationalising the denominator, the surface area of pyramids and cones, the volume of pyramids and cones, and the surface area and volume of spheres. There are 15 multiple-choice questions, from easy to challenge. Allow about 25 minutes, with no notes and no calculator: every answer is exact, so leave π and surds in your answers. Read each question carefully, look at the diagram when there is one, and check whether it asks for a surface area or a volume.

questions.topic: Surface area of pyramids and cones
questions.prompt: The square pyramid in the diagram has base edges of 12 cm and a slant height of 15 cm. Find its surface area.
questions.explanation: Base 144 + four triangles 4 × 90 = 360, so SA = 504 cm².

mistakes.A: Step 2: each triangle is ½ × 12 × 15 = 90 cm². You left out the ½.
mistakes.B: Step 3: add the square base, 12 × 12 = 144 cm².
mistakes.D: Step 2: there are four triangular faces, not one.

mistakes.A: Step 3: a cone is one-third of a cylinder. Multiply by ⅓.
mistakes.B: Step 1: the radius must be squared: 2² = 4.
mistakes.C: Step 3: the cone formula uses ⅓, not ½.

questions.prompt: Rationalise the denominator of 5/√10 and simplify.

mistakes.A: Step 2: the bottom becomes √10 × √10 = 10. Divide by it.
mistakes.C: Step 3: 5√10/10 means 5 ÷ 10 = ½, giving √10/2. You divided 10 by 5.
mistakes.D: Step 1: the top is 5, not √5. Multiply 5 by √10.

questions.prompt: The right-angled triangle in the diagram has a hypotenuse of 9 cm and one shorter side of 3 cm. Find the exact length of the other side x, in simplest surd form.
steps: 9 cm is the hypotenuse, so x² = 9² − 3².

mistakes.A: Step 1: 9 cm is the hypotenuse, so subtract: x² = 81 − 9. Adding gives √90.
mistakes.B: Step 1: you subtracted the sides. Subtract their squares.

questions.prompt: The triangle in the diagram has an area of 20 cm² and a base of 2√5 cm. Find its exact height h, with a rational denominator.

mistakes.A: Step 1: area = ½ × base × h, so h = 2 × 20 ÷ 2√5. You left out the first 2.

questions.prompt: A cone has a volume of 75π cm³ and a perpendicular height of 9 cm. Find its radius.
questions.explanation: ⅓ × π × r² × 9 = 75π, so 3r² = 75, r² = 25 and r = 5 cm.

mistakes.B: Step 3: r² = 25, so r = √25. Take the square root.
mistakes.C: Step 2: the cone formula has ⅓: ⅓ × 9 = 3, so 3r² = 75. You used 9r² = 75.
mistakes.D: Steps 2–3: you left out the ⅓ (9r² = 75) and did not take the square root.

questions.prompt: The outside of the silo in the diagram (its curved wall and dome, but not the floor) is to be painted. It is a cylinder of radius 2 m and height 6 m with a hemisphere on top. Find the area to be painted, in terms of π.

mistakes.A: Step 1: the dome is half a sphere, so its curved area is 2πr² = 8π, not 4πr² = 16π.
mistakes.C: Step 3: the floor is not painted, so leave out the base circle, 4π.
mistakes.D: Step 1: the dome’s curved surface is 2πr² = 8π, not πr² = 4π.

questions.prompt: A cone with radius 6 cm and height 8 cm is drilled out of a solid cylinder with the same radius and height. Find the volume that is left, in terms of π.
questions.explanation: Cylinder π × 36 × 8 = 288π; cone ⅓ × 288π = 96π; left over 288π − 96π = 192π cm³ (that is, ⅔ of the cylinder).

mistakes.A: Step 3: that is the cone that was removed. Subtract it from the cylinder.
mistakes.B: Step 3: the cone is removed, so subtract its volume, don’t add it.
mistakes.C: Step 2: the cone is ⅓ of the cylinder, not ½.

questions.explanation: Rationalise each: 1/(2 − √3) = 2 + √3 and 1/(2 + √3) = 2 − √3, because each denominator times its conjugate is 4 − 3 = 1. Sum = 4.
steps: Multiply each fraction by its conjugate: the bottoms become 4 − 3 = 1.

mistakes.C: Step 2: the √3 terms are +√3 and −√3, so they cancel; the 2s add to 4.
mistakes.D: You added the tops and the bottoms (2 ÷ 4). Fractions need a common denominator.

questions.topic: Surface area of pyramids and cones
questions.prompt: A square pyramid has all eight edges equal to 6 cm, as in the diagram, so each face is an equilateral triangle. Find its exact surface area.
questions.explanation: Face height √(36 − 9) = √27 = 3√3. Each face ½ × 6 × 3√3 = 9√3; four faces 36√3; plus base 36. SA = (36 + 36√3) cm².
steps: Each face is an equilateral triangle; its height is √(6² − 3²) = √27 = 3√3 cm.
One face = ½ × 6 × 3√3 = 9√3 cm²; four faces = 36√3 cm².

mistakes.A: Step 2: each face is ½ × 6 × 3√3 = 9√3 cm². You left out the ½.
mistakes.C: Step 3: add the square base, 6 × 6 = 36 cm².
mistakes.D: Step 1: 6 cm is the sloping edge, not the slant height of a face. Find the face height: √(6² − 3²).
